text.p: LME aluminium pushed higher to a bullish finish on Wednesday while copper and nickel eased off their peaks as players locked in profits.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index was 0.36 points lower at 242.02.

Aluminium surged during the last few mintues of the afternoon kerb and ended at a fresh seven month high of $1,590, the strongest since May 31, 1996. The technical outlook was positive after three month prices gapped higher in the morning, analyst William Adams of broker Rudolf Wolff said. "The close above $1,580 is very positive," he said, adding that charts were showing a reverse head and shoulders pattern. The long-term target was now around $1,800, with the first resistance level coming in at $1,609, Adams said. Stocks have remained stubbornly high at just under one million tonnes and have been on the rise again after putting in a series of declines from mid-November to mid-December.

Copper marched up to a high of $2,253 earlier in the day on nearby tightness and positive charts, but when prices failed to breach resistance they drifted back on profit taking to close the afternoon kerb at $2,240, up $19. The market on Tuesday shrugged off an increase in LME stocks, when data showed the bulk was in Singapore and was unlikely to help allieviate shortages in Europe and the US. The premium of cash over three months metal firmed again on Wednesday, ending the day at $135/$138, up $15 from Tuesday.

Nickel also came off its peak after blistering New Year gains that saw it add over $800 or 12 percent in a few days. Profit-takers came in on Wednesday after prices stalled at a peak of $7,250, and prices ended the day at $7,115, up $35 on the day.
Tin held within its sideways trading band over the past month, adding $20 to $5,800. Chartist Harry Creates of broker AMT pegged important support at $5,745 and key resistance at $5,880.
Lead declined $9 to $695 and zinc lost $7 to $1,065.

New York precious metals futures remained sharply lower at midday Wednesday, with fund selling seen early in gold, although silver was finding some support, traders said. "After the initial sell-off, we saw some further selling by overseas banks in gold, but the trade is buying silver on the dips," Rosko Futures floor trader John Rosko said. COMEX February gold was down $3.10 at $356.60 an ounce after setting a contract low of $355.30. In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $355.20/70 after gold fixed at $356.60 in London Wednesday afternoon, up from the morning fix of $355.80, the lowest since Oct 6, 1993.

CBOT wheat futures were modestly higher at midsession on concerns over the potential for cold weather damage to the U.S. wheat crop and export demand, CBOT traders said. "The weather, that is what's keeping the wheat higher," said one CBOT floor trader. "Wheat is on fire." At 1059 CST, CBOT wheat was one to four cents per bushel higher, with March up 3-3/4 cent at $3.96, and May up four cents at $3.74.

CSCE world sugar futures were a touch weaker at midday, pressured by mixed speculative and industry buying, market sources said. After three successive days of volatile trading, prices hovered well inside of yesterday's range. Commodity funds, who were active on both sides of the market earlier this week, were barely heard from this morning, dealers said. At 1154 EST, March futures were down 0.03 cent a lb, at 10.93, having ranged from 10.85 to 10.97. May futures, which were well bid by the funds into Tuesday's close, were off 0.05 to 11.00.

NYMEX February crude oil futures, led by heating oil, took an upturn Wednesday afternoon amid a change in weather forecasts calling for colder weather and upcoming refinery turnarounds. "The weather is a factor and there are still refinery turnarounds (in the U.S. Gulf) coming up early this month," said one New York Harbor trader. Traders reported forecasters have recast their six to 10-day outlook from cold to very cold, with temperatures 15-degrees to 20-degrees Fahrenheit below normal in the Midwest. February crude oil support, meanwhile, was pegged at between $25.65 to $25.70 a barrel with resistance at about $26.45 a barrel.
